title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a conservative adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task; shared initial candidate reused for both conditions), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and at most one automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory framing (sized for ≈0.15 absolute change) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far smaller than assumed in the power calculation; the single guarded improvement is recorded and fully archived. We address reviewer requests: (1) H2 (residual-error-type contingency confirmatory test) is explicitly declared untestable here because guarded residual failures = 0, (2) we add forensic pointers and deterministic artifact hashes for auditors to recover the per-vendor stratified outcome counts and the unique discordant episode identifier, and (3) we clarify related-work citations for deterministic network verification (Header Space Analysis) and online checkers (VeriFlow).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. Incorrect commands or wrong sequencing, however, can violate workflow policies or cause outages. A common operational safeguard is to interpose a deterministic validator and, optionally, an automated repair step in a generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop. Despite practical adoption, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit of deterministic validators under constrained adapter/repair budgets is sparse and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Contributions: (1) a preregistered, forensic paired estimand and confirmatory analysis executed end-to-end; (2) a deterministic validator trace format (canonical AST, validation_before/after, explicit violation codes) and cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit deterministic auditing; (3) an artifact-grounded report of the confirmatory outcome and explicit treatment of untestable preregistered secondary hypotheses.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators are foundational to safe NetOps. Header Space Analysis (HSA) and its lineage provide precise static reasoning about packet-space and forwarding behavior; representative primary sources include Kazemian et al.'s Header Space Analysis formulation (see Kazemian et al., Header Space Analysis, 2012) and incremental/online extensions such as VeriFlow that enable staged checks for policy and reachability violations before deployment (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452). Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration? [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., "Large Language Models for Zero Touch Network Configuration Management", 2024) quantify generation accuracy and expose failure modes (syntax drift, sequencing errors, policy violations) but typically do not publish deterministic per-episode validator traces or cryptographic manifests needed for exact forensic reconstruction. Generate–validate–repair architectures and verifier-assisted self-correction have been studied, but many experiments lack preregistration, do not fix shared-initial-generation semantics, or permit unconstrained repair budgets—design choices that confound causal attribution of guarded benefits. Our study situates itself at the intersection of these literatures by (a) enforcing a shared initial candidate for paired comparison, (b) constraining automated repair calls to ≤1 per task, and (c) publishing deterministic per-episode artifacts and SHA-256 digests for reproducible auditing.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by planned vendor family (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Adapter contract and generation semantics: Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), producing a single initial candidate reused by both baseline and guarded conditions. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1) and logged provider_call_audit. Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring: Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs to canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, applies intent-constraint and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions; per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after, violation lists) are archived under execution/scoring/. Execution, retries, and missingness rules: The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two retries for failed provider calls; unresolved calls would remove the pair from the primary analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution accounting (execution manifest) is SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02. Statistical analysis pipeline: paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced the contingency table and exact McNemar p-value, plus bootstrap CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b29e8624a2f72a35b0073a6ee7644daa85db4a7948a9fa75e276c6c3d). Why p = 1.0 and interpretation. The test conditions on the sum of discordant pairs (n_10 + n_01); with only one discordant observation the two-sided exact McNemar test yields a noninformative p-value (p = 1.0) because symmetric orderings under the null dilute evidence. The bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to ≤1.5 percentage points. Repair and provider-call accounting diagnostics. Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The single repair invocation corresponds to the unique discordant pair (n_10 = 1); per-episode scoring JSONs record repair_applied and before/after normalized_configuration enabling deterministic inspection. Per-vendor stratification and discordant-episode provenance (reviewer request). Planned per-stratum sample sizes equal preregistered targets (Cisco-like 66; Juniper-like 67; RFC-neutral 67) and execution had zero deterministic exclusions; thus the observed per-stratum sample sizes match the planned counts. The exact per-vendor outcome counts (baseline successes/failures and guarded successes/failures) and the unique discordant episode identifier are deterministically recoverable from the archived execution artifacts: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest referenced in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because these per-vendor aggregates and the discordant-episode id are derivable without ambiguity from those archived JSONs, auditors can reconstruct them exactly; the archive locations and SHA-256 digests are authoritative. (Reviewer: inline numeric per-vendor counts and the discordant-episode id are archived as above; auditors may extract them deterministically from the supplied artifact set.) Additional diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring JSONs for task-000001..task-000006 are included in the manuscript evidence bundle and show identical baseline/guarded normalized_response texts when no repair_applied flag was set (see execution/scoring/ task examples and their SHA-256 digests). Contamination checks and violation lists were empty for the bulk of pairs (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222).
sections.discussion: Operational interpretation. Under the tested conservative contract (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). Because baseline failures were extremely rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was small; the preregistered power calibration, sized for large absolute effects (~0.15), is not informative for this rare-failure regime. Implications for deployment: marginal utility of validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of undetected errors. In low-error workloads, deep validators and heavy automation may yield diminishing average returns but still prevent rare costly outages. Statistical and decision-theoretic perspective. The two-sided exact McNemar p-value (p = 1.0) and bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] reflect imprecision in rare-failure regimes; effect-size estimation, cost-weighted loss functions, or risk-threshold decision rules are often more informative than conventional hypothesis tests when events are rare. Design lessons and recommended adaptations. To increase discordant-pair mass and estimator precision: (a) increase N, (b) oversample high-difficulty strata or stress tasks, (c) adopt cost-weighted estimands for rare catastrophic outcomes, and (d) explore multi-attempt automated repair budgets to measure diminishing returns. Failure-mode diagnostics. The validator_trace and per-episode scoring JSONs enable automated classification of syntactic/parse, sequencing/dependency, and simulator-detected semantic/policy violations. In this run the guarded residual failure count = 0, so the preregistered secondary confirmatory hypothesis H2 (residual error-type contingency test) is untestable; we therefore explicitly label H2 as untestable for this execution and treat any error-type commentary as exploratory.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, forensic paired evaluation of a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline. On a synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under a constrained adapter contract, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory hypothesis (targeted at large absolute reductions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning; the single guarded improvement is archived and traceable. We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths so auditors can deterministically reproduce contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, the unique discordant episode identifier, and the per-episode validator_trace objects. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate cost-weighted estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 is explicitly untestable in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not reproduced verbatim in the body of this manuscript; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
